## Result

- Skill: delivery-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Package members: exact revised registered primary plan docs/plans/2026-09-10-release-validation-integration.md.
- Upstream review ID: design-review-r2 for unchanged Release/guidance contract; unchanged adopted CLI model supplies the scoped existing CLI-SR10/18/23 discovery behavior.
- Review ID and round: delivery-review-r4, round4.
- Traceability result: adequate existing M1 Release allocation plus bounded current-work discovery restoration and direct proof.
- Material findings: none new; original rvi-delivery-f1 remains resolved.
- Correction targets: none.
- Recording status: recorded upon successful targeted save.
- Open blockers: none to this Delivery decision; actual implementation and final PR/main evidence remain pending.
- Immediate next stage: return to route for existing M1 correction and assessment.
- Claim limitations: no implementation approval, CI pass, final Verify/PR/publication claim.

## Independent complete-plan assessment

Original independent Delivery assessor authored none of the plan, Design or engineering. Read the entire revised primary plan, its exact delta, current Release Design basis and the existing CLI Current-work discovery and retired inputs section, with actual workflow-context/classifier/test placement. Current Design r2 governing model/guidance identities remain unchanged. Its old plan identity is contextual allocation history, not another normative Design member; this review establishes the revised primary plan rather than claiming that old contextual identity matches. Preserve Delivery r3 original/stale.

The reported real main failure exposed an existing current-work discovery defect, not a new product requirement. CLI-SR23 requires structural classification without interpreting historical payloads, excludes sole YAML and empty/noncurrent directories, and reserves change-ID grammar for current candidates while retaining unsafe-path rejection. Actual workflow-context currently checks safeId before invoking the classifier, so a long historical directory blocks discovery before its archival classification. The plan now names this bounded restoration and its exact owning rules; it does not weaken grammar for current or explicitly selected records.

Implementation remains one M1 because the correction is a necessary compatibility dependency of the already-required direct main graph. No historical directories or records may be renamed, deleted, rewritten or parsed to make the gate pass. Safe path inspection must precede classification; both manifests, present malformed JSON, reserved v2 residue and symlinks remain errors. The existing multiple-invalid-ID test currently creates empty directories, which are noncurrent by contract; giving that rejection fixture actual current manifests preserves its intended current-ID protection while adding separate long-name archive/noncurrent exclusion proof. This is a test-input correction under the existing owner, not a waived negative case.

The plan explicitly allocates CLI-SR10/18/23 to long historical-name exclusion, invalid current IDs, mixed manifests, reserved residue, unsafe paths and explicit invalid selection. Its command node --test packages/rigorloop/test/workflow-context.test.js exercises the existing public discovery surface; actual main discovery gate remains required. Shared classifier ordering and no-decoding intent are feasible without any new runtime reader, migration or discovery service. No new CLI Design amendment is needed because the selected observable behavior exactly restores the current table.

## Retained full delivery and proof

All existing Release M1 obligations remain: shared isolated preparation before selected PR and direct main runners; every direct gate/order and failure propagated; actual package overlay and exact checked subject; unmodified original checkout; current fixtures derived from tested package with historical/incompatible cases fixed; CI-only publication rejection and hosted increment enforcement; unknown/malformed input and stale identity rejection. The current plan amendment removes none of those requirements. Prior r3 analysis of the offline/public split remains applicable as allocation reasoning, not runtime success.

Focused release/selector/discovery proof must precede both actual PR and main commands on the same newly committed final source. Earlier partial runs remain incomplete/failed: PR12/13 does not establish all-check success, and main stopping at discovery does not establish later gate results. The prepared-C head correction and plan navigation correction are implementation/integration subjects for Code Review; this review does not approve them merely because the author reports a focused pass. Rebuild current candidate proof when code or package inputs change; preserve current source and historical identities.

Independent M1 review and separate fresh final whole-change Code Review still precede distinct Verify. No new work entry, broader cleanup, provider policy, publication path or remote setup change is selected. Failure recovery restores the bounded correction slice together; never bypass discovery or skip a required main check. External npm setup and final release approval remain separately owned.

## Checks and handoff

Actually performed complete plan/delta read, current exact model/guidance subject checks, scoped existing CLI contract and actual classifier/caller/test inspection, primary subject refresh and targeted recording. No runtime test or engineering edit performed by this Delivery review. Scoped record-store validation and diff checks follow persistence. Return to route; no work initialization or mutable lifecycle transition is made.
independence_basis: Original independent nonauthor assessed complete revised plan and unchanged adopted CLI discovery boundary; no plan/model/engineering/work edits.
